valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E: FY2027 adjusted EPS viewed at the Nov 2027 target date, USD per share of the US common listing (no ADR conversion). Q3 2026 adjusted EPS was $26.93 on an R&M margin of $45.70/bbl, a cyclical peak (about 278M diluted shares implied by $7.4B net income / $26.59). Cases assume margins normalize from the peak; EPS and multiples are my assumptions, not company guidance.

bear.driver: Refining margins revert to mid-cycle, Q4 utilization 95%

base.driver: Margins stay elevated but ease, buybacks and asset sales ($4.2B) support per-share earnings

bull.driver: Tight product markets persist, near-peak margins

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS $28 the close of $414.65 implies 14.8x; the published consensus target near $385 implies 13.7x on base EPS or EPS about $32 at 12x
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $28 (6.8 pp of the close)
valuation.watch_metric: R&M margin per barrel and crude utilization versus the Q3 level of $45.70/bbl and 100%

analyst_notes: Only three named calls were verified (Jefferies, Goldman, TD Cowen, all raises in Jul-Aug 2026), none after the Nov 3 earnings; horizons are undocumented so they carry no weight. Benzinga showed a consensus target near $385 (Nov 6). The base case sits below that mainly because it assumes margins and EPS fall from the Q3 peak.
